analysis:
The only changed file is docs/architecture/inference.md. It has a date bump (line 3), a GLM-5-Next video paragraph rewrite (head ~810-813), and a sentence edit (head ~829). The reviewed units show a base excerpt covering Flint/Bonsai docs (base 2366-2597) and a head excerpt covering the file start through about line 415. The changed GLM lines themselves (head 810-829) are not visible in either supplied unit. I relied on the patch excerpt for them, so I could not verify surrounding source for those lines.

The change is documentation-only. It records that a GLM-5-Next video track is read frame by frame in presentation order, with frame i timed at i / nominalFrameRate. As a result, variable-frame-rate tracks are indexed instead of refused as a deterministic 400. Nothing in the diff changes code, so no control is demonstrably weakened here. If the corresponding code change is in the PR (it is not in this batch), it would loosen an input-validation gate in the media-decode path (TB-003/TB-007 area, similar to T-050). Integration should check three things in the GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset code. First, the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes) must still bound memory on VFR inputs. Second, a zero or invalid nominalFrameRate must be handled safely, with no divide-by-zero and no unbounded frame count. Third, the media-reservation charge (GLM5NextVisionBudget.videoTokenCeiling) must remain valid for VFR tracks. The docs state that media requests are excluded from prefix lookup and capture, so the T-041 cross-tenant cache exposure is unaffected. I found no new attack surface, trust-boundary change, or threat-model invalidation from the docs alone. The code that backs this doc change is outside the supplied evidence, so I request deeper review of it.
